items.headline: Apple Unveils M6 and M5 Ultra Chips With Major AI Compute Gains
items.summary: Apple introduced the M6, its first chip built on a 2-nanometer process, alongside the quad-die M5 Ultra with up to 80 GPU cores and 512GB of unified memory. The company says the new silicon delivers nearly 30 percent more peak GPU compute for AI than the M5 and much faster prompt processing for on-device large language models. The chips debut in a new Mac mini and Mac Studio, pushing toward running frontier AI models locally for creative professionals.

items.headline: Australia's ARIA Charts Will Exclude Fully AI-Generated Songs
items.summary: The Australian Recording Industry Association announced that tracks created primarily by AI will no longer be eligible for its official music charts or the ARIA Music Awards, starting with the chart dated August 31, 2026. Recordings that use generative AI in a supporting role can still qualify if they are substantially human-made and raise no manipulation concerns. ARIA is also introducing an AI-Generated versus AI-Assisted labeling system based on a global standard the music industry agreed on in July.

items.headline: Adobe Firefly Adds Generative Music, Speech and Sound Effects
items.summary: Adobe made Firefly's audio tools generally available, rounding out its creative AI studio with Generate Music, Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects alongside its existing image and video tools. The Firefly Music Model produces original tracks tuned to a video's length and mood and is designed for commercial use without the risk of copyright takedowns. The update pushes Firefly further toward an all-in-one generative suite for video editors and content creators.

items.headline: UK Cinemas Move to Restrict Camera-Enabled Smart Glasses
items.summary: British cinema operators are introducing policies to prohibit or restrict camera-equipped smart glasses, including Meta's AI-powered eyewear, citing film piracy and privacy concerns. The UK Cinema Association said the rules vary by venue rather than following one industry-wide standard, following courts in England and Wales this month barring the glasses over recording restrictions. Operators acknowledged the devices can also aid moviegoers with accessibility needs, complicating a blanket ban.

items.headline: California AG Accuses Paramount of Bad Faith in Warner Bros. Talks
items.summary: California's attorney general called off settlement discussions with Paramount Skydance, accusing the company of leaking details of confidential talks and misrepresenting them publicly. The rift comes as regulators continue reviewing the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger, which saw Paramount outbid Netflix for the media giant earlier in 2026. The standoff adds a fresh legal complication to a deal that still requires federal antitrust sign-off.
